themes.label: Decrees
themes.rationale: The text is a formal Athenian decree (psephisma) passed by the council and people to regulate public standards.
themes.quote: ἀναγράψαι δὲ τό̣[δε] τὸ [ψήφισμ]α [εἰ]ς στήλας λιθ[ίν]α[ς]

themes.label: Laws and Regulations
themes.rationale: The inscription establishes comprehensive legal regulations for commercial weights and measures and defines penalties for violations.
themes.quote: οἱ ἄρχοντες ἐξεταζέτωσαν πρὸς τὸ σύμβολον τὸ ἐν τῆι σκιάδι

themes.label: Sacred Laws and Rules
themes.rationale: The decree includes religious sanctions, such as fines payable to Demeter and Kore, and involves the Hierophant in enforcement at Eleusis.
themes.quote: ὀ[φ]ειλέτω ἱερὰς̣ τῆι Δήμητρι [κ]αὶ τῆι Κόρηι δραχμὰς χιλίας

themes.label: Inventories
themes.rationale: The text mandates a formal inventory and handover process for the official weights and measures between outgoing and incoming public slaves.
themes.quote: μετ ἀναγραφῆς π̣άν[τα] τὰ [μέτρα καὶ σταθμά]

themes.label: Stele
themes.rationale: The decree explicitly orders its own publication on stone stelae to be placed where the weights are kept.
themes.quote: ἀναγράψαι δὲ τό̣[δε] τὸ [ψήφισμ]α [εἰ]ς στήλας λιθ[ίν]α[ς]

themes.label: Marble
themes.rationale: As a monumental Athenian decree from the Akropolis, it was inscribed on marble, though the text simply specifies stone.

themes.label: Fragmentary
themes.rationale: The text contains numerous lacunae and reconstructed sections, indicating the physical state of the stone is not intact.
themes.quote: [τοῦ μέτρου ὡς ἐλάττονος ὄντος, οἱ ἄρχοντες ἐξεταζέτωσαν]

persons.name: Diodorus son of Theophilus of Halae
persons.role: Official appointed for the construction of weights and measures

persons.name: Hierophant
persons.role: Religious official at Eleusis responsible for enforcement

rationale: This significant Athenian decree, dating to approximately 120 BC, provides a detailed regulatory framework for the standardization of weights and measures (metrology) in Attica. It establishes official standards to be kept in key locations (the Skias in the Agora, Piraeus, Eleusis, and the Akropolis) and defines the technical specifications for various units like the mina, talent, and choinix. The law distinguishes between commercial and silver weight systems and sets specific measures for various commodities such as nuts, olives, and figs. It also outlines a strict enforcement regime involving various magistrates, the Council of 600, and the Areopagus, with penalties ranging from corporal punishment for slaves to heavy fines for free citizens and officials.
